claims.evidence: Counted CAP-01 through CAP-15; matches deep-depth 8-15 range.

claims.claim: The librarian skill was not available in this run
claims.evidence: Line 7 states librarian skill is not available; the output adapts by listing what to search instead of invoking it. Consistent with a non-interactive eval harness without skill tools wired in.

claims.claim: This run conducted no research itself
claims.evidence: Line 615 explicitly says 'this run did not conduct research'; no web/search activity reflected in output, only flagged topics.
Reviewed all 15 flows; they describe behavior/decisions, using abstract roles (payment gateway, object storage, CDN) rather than named tech, code, or architecture.

uncertainties: Run noted librarian skill unavailable, so existing-knowledge check was documented as guidance rather than executed
workarounds: Made explicit Key Assumptions (line 35) because clarifying questions could not be asked in a non-interactive run

suggestions.assertion: Checks for existing knowledge via librarian skill before starting
suggestions.reason: This assertion can only be partially verified from the output. The skill cannot truly invoke librarian in the eval harness, so it documents intent instead of performing the check. Both runs are graded on a deferred-tools environment; consider clarifying whether 'documents the librarian check' satisfies this, or whether an actual tool call is required (which the harness may not support).

suggestions.assertion: Covers user account/onboarding capabilities for both sides
suggestions.reason: Buyer-side onboarding is only implied via an assumed external identity system, while seller onboarding gets a full CAP. The assertion passes generously; consider specifying whether buyer onboarding needs its own capability to make this discriminating.

No assertion checks for the 'Existing Knowledge' section that OUTPUT_FORMAT prescribes (and which the with_skill run produced). Adding one would better discriminate the prescribed structure from a generic breakdown.

eval_feedback.overall: Assertions are strong and discriminating for structure, CAP-NN format, delegation, and content coverage. The with_skill output passes all 37 cleanly. Two assertions (librarian check, both-side onboarding) pass somewhat generously and could be tightened.
